entities.summary:
Jan of Głogów was a notable Polish polyhistor at the turn of the Middle Ages and Renaissance—a philosopher, geographer and astronomer at the University of Krakow.

Born in 1445 in Głogów, a small town in the Duchy of Legnica, Jan of Głogów was a polymath who excelled in various fields, including philosophy, geography, and astronomy. He was a student of the University of Krakow, where he studied under the tutelage of prominent scholars of his time.

Jan of Głogów's most notable contribution was his work on the geography of Poland, which was considered a masterpiece in his lifetime. His book, "Geographia Poloniae", provided a detailed description of the geography, climate, and natural resources of Poland, and was used as a reference by later scholars.

Jan of Głogów's legacy extended beyond his scientific contributions. He was also a patron of the arts and a member of the Polish nobility, and his family played an important role in the history of the region.

"The earth is a book, and those who do not travel read only one page." - Jan of Głogów

This quote encapsulates Jan of Głogów's love of exploration and learning, which drove him to explore the world and record his findings.

Jan of Głogów's work had a lasting impact on the development of geography and astronomy in Poland, and his legacy continues to be celebrated by scholars and historians today.

The University of Krakow, where Jan of Głogów studied and taught, remains one of the oldest and most prestigious universities in Poland, and a testament to the enduring legacy of this remarkable polymath.
